questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests sliding-window knowledge, practical data structures, and amortized reasoning relevant to real-time analytics.

## Key Concepts

- Sliding window
- Amortized analysis
- Hashmap counters
- Circular buffer

## Code Example

```python
class DistinctWindow:
    def __init__(self, W):
        self.W = W
        self.buf = [None]*W
        self.left = 0
        self.right = 0
        self.size = 0
        self.counts = {}

    def append(self, v):
        if self.size == self.W:
            old = self.buf[self.left]
            self.buf[self.left] = None
            self.left = (self.left + 1) % self.W
            self.size -= 1
            if old is not None:
                c = self.counts[old]
                if c == 1:
                    del self.counts[old]
                else:
                    self.counts[old] = c - 1
        self.buf[self.right] = v
        self.right = (self.right + 1) % self.W
        self.size += 1
        self.counts[v] = self.counts.get(v, 0) + 1

    def distinctCount(self):
        return len(self.counts)
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How does performance change if W is very large but few unique values exist? Any memory optimizations?
- How would you adapt to a dynamic window size W' that changes over time without recomputing from scratch?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design dynamic range properties with batched updates and amortized analysis, leveraging a segment-tree style approach for real-time run-length maintenance.

## Key Concepts

- Segment tree storing (length, pref1, suf1, best1)
- Merge to propagate cross-boundary runs
- Amortized batch updates vs per-item cost
- Cache-friendly iterative layout

## Code Example

```python
class Node:
    def __init__(self, length=0, pref=0, suf=0, best=0):
        self.length = length
        self.pref = pref
        self.suf = suf
        self.best = best

def merge(a, b):
    length = a.length + b.length
    pref = a.length if a.pref == a.length else a.pref
    if a.pref == a.length:
        pref = a.length + b.pref
    suf = b.length if b.suf == b.length else b.suf
    if b.suf == b.length:
        suf = b.length + a.suf
    best = max(a.best, b.best, a.suf + b.pref)
    return Node(length, pref, suf, best)
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you extend to range flips (set to 0/1) or range updates? 
- How does performance adapt when B approaches n or L is near n?

## Why This Is Asked
Assesses ability to pick a compact streaming distinct-counter and reason about trade-offs between memory, accuracy, and update time; tests understanding of probabilistic data structures for real-time analytics.

## Key Concepts
- HyperLogLog: probabilistic distinct counting using registers.
- Space-accuracy trade-off: m = 2^p.
- Update: O(1) average; query: O(1) to get estimate.
- Comparison to exact: O(M) memory, slower with large M.

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudocode sketch for HLL insert
function hllAdd(x, hash, registers, m){
  const h = hash64(x)
  const j = h >>> (64 - p) // top p bits
  const w = h << p | 1 // remaining bits
  const rank = leadingZeros64(w) + 1
  if (registers[j] < rank) registers[j] = rank
}
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question probes ability to design a sliding-window frequency data structure with bounded memory and predictable per-element cost, a common requirement in real-time analytics at scale.

## Key Concepts
- Sliding window maintenance
- Frequency map with eviction
- Top-k extraction
- Memory vs time trade-offs

## Code Example
```javascript
class SlidingWindowTopK {
  constructor(W) { this.W=W; this.q=[]; this.freq=new Map(); }
  add(v){ this.q.push(v); this.freq.set(v,(this.freq.get(v)||0)+1); if(this.q.length>this.W){ const o=this.q.shift(); const c=this.freq.get(o)-1; if(c===0) this.freq.delete(o); else this.freq.set(o,c); } }
  topK(k=3){ const arr=[...this.freq.entries()]; arr.sort((a,b)=>b[1]-a[1]); return arr.slice(0,k).map(e=>e[0]); }
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you support dynamic window resizing? 
- How would you optimize topK for large W?
